facts: Choose a side as the base. Its height is measured at a right angle from that base to the opposite corner.
The height may meet the base outside the triangle. Extend the base in a straight line to find it.
Use the height for the chosen base. A slanted side is not that height unless it meets the base at a right angle.
Area is measured in square units: cm$^{2}$, m$^{2}$.
steps: Identify the base and its perpendicular height (at a right angle to the base or its extension).
Multiply base $\times$ height, then halve the result.
Write the answer with squared units.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The base is $11\text{ cm}$. Its perpendicular height is $4\text{ cm}$. The slanted $5\text{ cm}$ side is not needed.

$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=11\times4\div2\\&=44\div2\\&=22\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

Use the actual $9\text{ cm}$ base, excluding its extension. The perpendicular height is $6\text{ cm}$, outside the triangle. The slanted $10\text{ cm}$ side is not needed.

$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=9\times6\div2\\&=54\div2\\&=27\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

Turn one copy around and join it to the other copy. The two equal triangles fill the parallelogram.

$\begin{align*}\text{Parallelogram area}&=13\times6\\&=78\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

Each triangle has half that area.

$\begin{align*}\text{Triangle area}&=78\div2\\&=39\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

For any triangle, multiply its base by its perpendicular height, then halve the result.

workedExamples.question_text: Triangle A has base $12\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $5\text{ cm}$. Triangle B has base $9\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $8\text{ cm}$. Which has the larger area, and by how many square centimetres?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Area of A}&=12\times5\div2\\&=30\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\text{Area of B}&=9\times8\div2\\&=36\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

$36-30=6$

Triangle B is larger by $6\text{ cm}^{2}$. Compare the areas, not just the base lengths.

Each smaller triangle uses its own base and the common perpendicular height.

$\begin{align*}\text{First area}&=7\times6\div2\\&=21\text{ m}^{2}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\text{Second area}&=11\times6\div2\\&=33\text{ m}^{2}\end{align*}$

$33-21=12$

The difference is $12\text{ m}^{2}$.

workedExamples.question_text: A triangular garden has base $11\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $4\text{ m}$. Find its area.
A triangular lawn has base $13\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $6\text{ m}$. Find its area.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The $24\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$ sides meet at a right angle. Use them as the base and height; the slanted side is not needed.

$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=24\times10\div2\\&=240\div2\\&=120\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

The student multiplied all three given lengths. Use only the base and its perpendicular height. The slanted $5\text{ cm}$ side is not needed.

$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=10\times4\div2\\&=40\div2\\&=20\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

Both triangles have base $12\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $7\text{ cm}$. Triangle B's height meets the extension of its base.

$\begin{align*}\text{Area of A}&=12\times7\div2\\&=84\div2\\&=42\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\text{Area of B}&=12\times7\div2\\&=84\div2\\&=42\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

Their bases and perpendicular heights are equal, so their areas are equal despite their different shapes.

foundation.question_text:
A rectangular block of land measuring $30\text{ m}$ long by $18\text{ m}$ wide is cut in half along a diagonal.
Find the area of each triangular block in $\text{m}^{2}$.
foundation.solution_text:
Each triangle has the same base and height as the rectangle.
$\text{Area}=\text{base}\times\text{height}\div2$
$=30\times18\div2$
$=270\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
A line from the top corner of a triangle divides its base into $9\text{ cm}$ and $15\text{ cm}$. Both smaller triangles have perpendicular height $8\text{ cm}$.
Find the difference between their areas in $\text{cm}^{2}$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{First area}=9\times8\div2$
$=36\text{ cm}^{2}$
$\text{Second area}=15\times8\div2$
$=60\text{ cm}^{2}$
$60-36=24$
The difference is $24\text{ cm}^{2}$.

mastery.question_text:
A triangle has a base of $17.6\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $9.5\text{ m}$. The height meets the straight-line extension of the base outside the triangle.
Find the area of the triangle in $\text{m}^{2}$.
mastery.solution_text:
Use the actual base and its perpendicular height, even though the height is outside the triangle.
$\text{Area}=17.6\times9.5\div2$
$=167.2\div2$
$=83.6\text{ m}^{2}$
